name: Caln Township
notes: 2023 is the latest audit on file. Finding 2023-002 is a material weakness with a modified compliance opinion; no repeat or questioned-cost flag. Short text limits judgment.

name: CITY OF COLONIAL HEIGHTS
notes: 2024-003 has a modified compliance opinion and is repeated from 2023-003. Management reports contract corrections, but the text does not establish that all issues were isolated and corrected; 2024-004 also repeats.

name: CITY OF EMPORIA
notes: 2024-010 is a repeated material weakness; 2024-011 through 2024-014 show additional procurement, payment approval, reporting and reconciliation failures.

name: CITY OF MARTINSVILLE
notes: 2025-002 is a material weakness, not repeated and without questioned costs; 2023-2024 have no federal findings. Staff turnover is mentioned, but the auditor describes a single-program reporting failure.

name: CITY OF ROANOKE
notes: 2025-003 and 2025-004 are repeated material weaknesses. Additional 2025 material weaknesses and modified compliance opinions affect several programs.

name: CITY OF STAUNTON, VIRGINIA
notes: Three findings in 2025 trigger medium. They concern eligibility approval, subaward information and report review; no serious, repeat or questioned-cost flags. The text does not clearly establish a shared systemic cause.

name: COUNTY OF BEDFORD, VIRGINIA
notes: 2025 and 2024 have no federal findings; the only in-window finding is 2023-001. Historical staff turnover alone does not establish a current systemic problem.

name: COUNTY OF CAROLINE, VIRGINIA
notes: 2024-003 repeats the procurement-policy finding from 2023-002, without material weakness, modified opinion or questioned costs. Countywide policy scope is concerning, but the text does not demonstrate broader finance-function failure.

name: COUNTY OF FLOYD
notes: Base medium: serious findings in 2025. Up one level for a procurement-control gap spanning CSLFRF and Child Nutrition: 2025-016 says "The County does not have a Uniform Guidance Procurement Manual." The text of 2025-017 reports a $186,000 understatement, but its questioned-cost flag is false.

name: County of Pittsylvania, Virginia
notes: 2025-001 is one non-serious, non-repeat finding with no questioned-cost flag. The serious 2023 finding does not alone make the latest audit high.

name: County of Pulaski, VA
notes: No federal findings in 2025 or 2024; only 2023-004 is in the window. Financial-statement material weaknesses are disclosed in all three years. The 2023 text is only a reporting requirement, so detail is limited; low is not a clean bill of health.

name: County of Scott, Virginia
notes: 2025 has no federal findings; 2024-005 has questioned costs. Financial-statement material weakness and material noncompliance remain disclosed in 2025; low follows the federal-findings rubric, not overall financial health.

name: County of Spotsylvania
notes: 2025-001 is a significant deficiency, not repeated, without questioned costs or modified opinion. The text identifies school reimbursement-review documentation gaps but does not clearly establish a wider systemic failure. Two 2023 submissions contain the same finding.

name: County of Tazewell, VA
notes: No federal findings in 2025 or 2024. Serious repeated 2023-003 is historical; its available text is only a program title. Financial-statement material weaknesses remain disclosed in 2025 and 2024; low is not a clean bill of health.

name: GREATER ROANOKE TRANSIT COMPANY
notes: 2024-005 is a repeated material weakness with a modified compliance opinion; 2023-007 was also serious. Cash-management deficiencies remain, with additional 2024 grant-closeout and procurement findings.

name: LEE COUNTY VA
notes: 2025 and 2024 have no federal findings; serious 2023-007 is historical. Financial-statement material weakness and material noncompliance are disclosed in all three years. Low is not an overall clean bill of health.

name: Middle Peninsula Planning District Commission
notes: Base medium: three material weaknesses in 2024. Up one level for systemic finance controls: 2024-001 says "did not have sufficient controls and redundancies to allow all accounting functions to be performed on a timely basis." Bank reconciliations, SEFA and audit submission are affected.

name: NEW RIVER VALLEY COMMUNITY SERVICES
notes: Base low: two non-serious, non-repeat 2024 findings without questioned costs. Up one level for systemic staffing failures affecting two programs: 2024-003 says "The Agency had two vacant positions in the Finance Department, one being the Senior Finance Director position for eight months."

name: Newport News Redevelopment and Housing Authority
notes: 2025-001 and 2025-002 are repeated material weaknesses with modified compliance opinions; 2025-002 also has $487 questioned costs. Multiple serious findings also appear in 2024.

name: Palm Beach County Housing Authority
notes: 2024-001 is a repeated material weakness with a modified compliance opinion and $12,428 questioned costs. Six additional findings include repeated deficiencies. Only 2024 is on file in the review window.

name: SCHOOL BOARD CITY OF RICHMOND
notes: 2025-003 is a repeated significant deficiency, without a material weakness, modified opinion or questioned costs. Earlier reporting findings are disputed by management; that dispute does not remove the latest repeat finding.

name: Scott County Redevelopment and Housing Authority
notes: 2025-001 is a repeated material weakness with $117,869 questioned costs; 2024-001 was also a material weakness with questioned costs. Planned HUD funding remedies do not demonstrate full correction.

name: SHENANDOAH AREA AGENCY ON AGING, INC
notes: Base medium: repeated significant deficiency 2024-002. Up one level for unreconciled reporting across three aging programs: "The 13th Aging Monthly Report was not reconciled to underlying financial records, resulting in unexplained differences between the report and trial balance provided as part of the audit."

name: THE WISE COUNTY HOUSING CORPORATION
notes: 2025 has no federal findings. The 2024 repeated material weakness and 2023 findings are earlier audits; no latest-year trigger or evidence of a current systemic problem is provided.

name: Town of Edinburg
notes: 2024-003 is a repeated material weakness. Management states "As of October 2024, the Town has adopted a Federal Procurement Policy." I did not downgrade: the missing-policy issue was broad, and the text does not establish that it was isolated and fully corrected before issuance.

name: TOWN OF ELKTON, VIRGINIA
notes: 2025-004 is repeated, but not flagged serious or questioned costs. Its prior reference says 2024-005, although the matching procurement issue appears as 2024-006; verify the reference. The repeat flag still supports medium.

name: Town of Pulaski
notes: 2025 has no federal findings and no going-concern flag; 2024-003 is historical and its text is only "Material Noncompliance". A going-concern doubt and financial-statement material weakness appear in 2023; material noncompliance remains disclosed in 2025. Low is not a clean bill of health.

name: Virginia Housing Development Authority
notes: 2025-001 and 2025-003 are repeated material weaknesses with modified compliance opinions and questioned costs; 2025-004 is also a repeated serious finding. Improvements are described as not fully operational for tested files.

name: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority
notes: 2025-003 is a repeated material weakness, also present in the restated 2024 audit. The same $2,385,715 timing error affects both years; concurrent discovery is not proof it was isolated and corrected. Use the restated 2024 submission, not the original no-findings submission.

name: WYTHEVILLE REDEVELOPMENT & HOUSING AUTHORITY
notes: Base medium: 2025-001 is a material weakness. Up one level for a systemic signature-control failure across Housing Choice and Mainstream Vouchers: "Approximately 44% of files selected for testing lacked the proper signatures for the time period covered by the audit." The cause cites executive/program turnover and inadequate training.
